newsitem.title: FINLAND: AMER K-OWNER SEES MOYNE DEAL HAPPENING - TV.
newsitem.headline: AMER K-OWNER SEES MOYNE DEAL HAPPENING - TV.

text.p: A representative of one of the four owners of sporting goods group Amer's K shares said on television on Friday morning he expected a rivalled deal to transfer control of Amer to Jonathan Brian Guinness to happen.

"With the current outlook (it will happen)," said Markku von Hertzen, managing director of the Finnish association for business graduates (SEFE) when asked whether the deal with Guinness, third Lord Moyne, would happen.

Amer's K shareholders agreed on June 2 to sell 1.1 million K shares for 301 million markka in an arrangement which would eventually give Guinness a 58 percent stake of votes in Amer and 4.6 percent of shares.

Guinness' bid was rivalled on Thursday when Finnish investment company Norvestia said it was interested in bidding for Amer with a starting point to offer "principally similar conditions" as in Guinness' model.
"We are so to speak engaged with Lord Moyne and then we should not look at other candidates," von Hertzen said.
SEFE owns 25 percent of the K shares.
